court: The European Court of Human Rights

facts.text: The applicant, Mr Salih Tekin, a Turkish citizen of Kurdish origin, was born in 1964 and lives in Diyarbakır. Prior to the events in question, he had been employed as a journalist for the newspaper Özgür Gündem.

anchor.surface_text: 7.  The applicant, Mr Salih Tekin, a Turkish citizen of Kurdish origin, was born in 1964 and lives in Diyarbakır. Prior to the events in question, he had been employed as a journalist for the newspaper Özgür Gündem.

facts.text: In February 1993, during a visit to his family in the hamlet of Yassıtepe, the applicant was arrested on suspicion of threatening village guards by gendarmes under Officer Harun Altın and taken to Derinsu gendarmerie headquarters.

anchor.surface_text: 8.  It was not disputed that in February 1993, during a visit to his family in the hamlet of Yassıtepe, the applicant was arrested, on suspicion of threatening village guards, by gendarmes under the command of Officer Harun Altın and taken to Derinsu gendarmerie headquarters.

facts.text: The applicant alleged his arrest took place on the morning of 15 February 1993, whereas the Government claimed it occurred on 17 February 1993.

anchor.surface_text: The applicant alleged that his arrest took place on the morning of 15 February 1993, whereas the Government claimed that it occurred on 17 February 1993.

facts.text: He was held at Derinsu until 19 February 1993, detained in a cell without lighting, bed or blankets, in sub-zero temperatures, fed only bread and water, and assaulted by gendarmes including Officer Altın.

anchor.surface_text: He alleged that during his time in custody there he was detained in a cell without any lighting, bed or blankets, in sub-zero temperatures, and fed with only bread and water. He claimed to have been assaulted in his cell by gendarmes, including Officer Altın.

facts.text: The Government denied ill-treatment, stating the security room was heated and his brothers were not allowed to join him.

anchor.surface_text: The Government denied that Mr Tekin had been ill-treated. They stated that it would have been impossible for the temperature in the security room to have dropped below freezing-point, since it was situated in the centre of the building and surrounded by other units heated by coal-burning stoves. They also denied that his brothers had been allowed to join him there.

facts.text: On the morning of 19 February 1993, the applicant was taken to Derik district gendarmerie headquarters and released the same day.

anchor.surface_text: On the morning of 19 February 1993, the applicant was taken to Derik district gendarmerie headquarters. He was released on the same day.

facts.text: He alleged torture at Derik through cold water, electric shocks and beatings to force a confession, and threats of death by district gendarmerie commander Musa Çitil.

anchor.surface_text: He alleged to have been tortured at Derik, through the application of cold water, electric shocks and beatings, with the purpose of forcing him to sign a confession statement. He claimed that the district gendarmerie commander, Musa Çitil, threatened him with death if he returned to the area.

facts.text: The Government contested that any ill-treatment had taken place at Derik.

anchor.surface_text: The Government contested that any ill-treatment had taken place.

facts.text: Prior to release, Mr Tekin was brought before public prosecutor Hasan Altun and complained of torture and ill-treatment at Derinsu and Derik; Mr Altun recorded but took no further action.

anchor.surface_text: Prior to being released, Mr Tekin was brought before the public prosecutor, Hasan Altun. It was not disputed that he complained to Mr Altun of having been tortured and ill-treated at both Derinsu and Derik. The applicant claimed in addition that he had handed Mr Altun a wet piece of cloth with which he had been blindfolded while being hosed with water. Mr Altun recorded these allegations, but took no further action in relation to them.

facts.text: The Supreme Council of Judges and Prosecutors decided to investigate Mr Altun's inaction, leading to disciplinary proceedings which had not yet concluded at the time of the judgment.

anchor.surface_text: The Supreme Council of Judges and Prosecutors consequently decided to commence an investigation into the reasons for Mr Altun’s inaction, which led to disciplinary proceedings being launched against him. During the hearing before the Court the Government confirmed that these proceedings had not yet been concluded.

facts.text: Mr Tekin returned to Diyarbakır on 20 February 1993, did not see a doctor after release, and lodged a complaint with the Human Rights Association the following week.

anchor.surface_text: Mr Tekin returned to Diyarbakır on 20 February 1993. He did not see a doctor after his release. The following week he lodged a complaint about his treatment with the Human Rights Association, which advised him to make an application to the Commission.

facts.text: The offence with which the applicant was charged fell within the competence of the National Security Courts; a Derik public prosecutor issued a decision of non-jurisdiction and referred the case to the Diyarbakır National Security Court.

anchor.surface_text: Since the offence with which the applicant was charged (see paragraph 8 above) fell within the competence of the National Security Courts (see paragraph 29 below), a Derik public prosecutor issued a decision of non-jurisdiction and referred the case to the Diyarbakır National Security Court.

facts.text: Following a hearing on 13 May 1993, the applicant was acquitted on 2 August 1993.

anchor.surface_text: Following a hearing on 13 May 1993, the applicant was acquitted on 2 August 1993.

facts.text: Following the Commission’s communication to the Government on 11 October 1993, the Ministry of Justice contacted the Derik public prosecutor’s office on 18 December 1993, informing it of the applicant’s complaints and opening a preliminary investigation.

anchor.surface_text: Following the Commission’s communication to the Government on 11 October 1993 of Mr Tekin’s application, the Ministry of Justice (International Law and External Relations General Directorate) contacted the public prosecutor’s office in Derik on 18 December 1993, informing it of the applicant’s complaints. A preliminary investigation was opened.

facts.text: Officer Altın was questioned on 20 April 1994 by a public prosecutor in Daday district at the request of the Derik public prosecutor.

anchor.surface_text: Officer Altın was questioned in connection with Mr Tekin’s allegations by a public prosecutor in Daday district on 20 April 1994, at the request of the Derik public prosecutor, Bekir Özenir.

facts.text: Mr Özenir issued a decision of non-prosecution on 4 May 1994 regarding officers Altın and Çitil due to lack of evidence beyond the applicant’s unsubstantiated allegations.

anchor.surface_text: Mr Özenir issued a decision of non-prosecution in relation to officers Altın and Çitil on 4 May 1994, on the grounds that there was no evidence that they had ill-treated or threatened Mr Tekin, other than the latter’s unsubstantiated allegations.

facts.text: The Ministry of Justice intervened to allow the applicant to appeal the non-prosecution decision and considered the alleged offences might fall under the Law on the Prosecution of Civil Servants, outside public prosecutor jurisdiction.

anchor.surface_text: However, this decision was not made final following the intervention of the Ministry of Justice, which took the view that Mr Tekin should be given the opportunity to file an appeal against it. Furthermore, because of the identities of the defendants and the nature of the allegations against them, the Ministry of Justice considered that the alleged offences might fall within the scope of the Law on the Prosecution of Civil Servants, over which the public prosecutor had no jurisdiction (see paragraph 30 below).

facts.text: A decision of non-jurisdiction was issued by the Derik public prosecutor’s office on 4 May 1995 and the case was referred to the Derik District Administrative Council.

anchor.surface_text: A decision of non-jurisdiction was subsequently issued by the Derik public prosecutor’s office on 4 May 1995 and the case was referred to the Derik District Administrative Council.

facts.text: On 14 July 1995, a statement was taken from Commander Çitil by a gendarmerie lieutenant-colonel.

anchor.surface_text: In this connection, on 14 July 1995, a statement was taken from Commander Çitil by a gendarmerie lieutenant-colonel.

facts.text: The Derik District Administrative Council submitted its summary investigation report to the Mardin provincial governor on 5 September 1995, which was referred to the Mardin Provincial Administrative Council on 12 September 1995.

anchor.surface_text: The Derik District Administrative Council submitted its summary investigation report to the office of the Mardin provincial governor on 5 September 1995. On 12 September 1995, this report was referred to the Mardin Provincial Administrative Council (see paragraph 30 below).

facts.text: The Mardin Provincial Administrative Council decided on 13 September 1995 that officers Altın and Çitil were exempt from public prosecution due to lack of evidence.

anchor.surface_text: The latter decided, on 13 September 1995, that, due to lack of evidence, officers Altın and Çitil were exempt from public prosecution.

facts.text: This decision was subject to automatic appeal to the Supreme Administrative Court, which confirmed the decision of non-prosecution.

anchor.surface_text: This decision was subject to an automatic appeal to the Supreme Administrative Court (see paragraph 30 below). The latter confirmed the decision of non-prosecution.

facts.text: The Commission conducted an investigation including witness statements, reports, documents, and hearings in Diyarbakır and Strasbourg, involving the applicant, his father, officers Altın and Çitil, and neighbours of the applicant’s father.

anchor.surface_text: The Commission conducted an investigation into the facts, with the assistance of the parties. It accepted written material, including witness statements, reports about Turkey, documents relating to the applicant’s detention at Derinsu and Derik gendarmerie headquarters and to the investigation on the domestic level into the applicant’s allegations, and a floor plan of Derinsu gendarmerie headquarters. In addition, three delegates of the Commission heard the oral evidence of seven witnesses in Diyarbakır on 8 November 1995 and a further hearing took place before the Commission in Strasbourg on 7 March 1996. The witnesses included the applicant, his father, Hacı Mehmet Tekin, officers Harun Altın and Musa Çitil, and three neighbours of the applicant’s father, Sinan Dinç, Mehmet Dinç and Halit Tutmaz, who alleged to have spoken to the applicant shortly after his release.

facts.text: The Commission was unable to determine the exact date of the applicant’s arrest or precise details of his treatment but was satisfied he had been kept in a cold and dark cell, blindfolded, and treated in a way leaving wounds and bruises.

anchor.surface_text: The Commission was unable to determine the date of the applicant’s arrest or the precise details of his treatment in custody. However, cautiously evaluating the evidence, the Commission was satisfied that the applicant had been kept in a cold and dark cell and blindfolded and treated in a way which left wounds and bruises on his body in connection with his interrogation.

holdings.text: Holds unanimously that there has been no violation of Article 2 of the Convention
holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court accepted the Commission's findings and concluded that the facts did not support interference with the applicant's right to life under Article 2.

holdings.text: Holds by six votes to three that there has been a violation of Article 3 of the Convention
holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court found that the applicant was held in inhuman and degrading conditions and subjected to treatment leaving wounds and bruises, amounting to a violation of Article 3.

holdings.text: Holds by eight votes to one that it is not necessary to consider the applicant6s complaints under Articles 5 7 1 and 6 7 1 of the Convention
holdings.reasoning_summary: The applicant did not pursue claims under Articles 5 § 1 and 6 § 1; therefore, the Court found no need to examine these complaints.

holdings.text: Holds unanimously that there has been no violation of Article 10 of the Convention
holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court found no evidence that the applicant's detention and treatment amounted to interference with his freedom of expression under Article 10.

holdings.text: Holds by seven votes to two that there has been a violation of Article 13 of the Convention
holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court found that the investigation into the applicant's allegations was inadequate and delayed, thus denying an effective domestic remedy under Article 13.

holdings.text: Holds unanimously that there has been no violation of Articles 14 or 18 of the Convention
holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court found no evidence substantiating the applicant's allegations of discrimination or breach of Article 18.

holdings.text: Holds by eight votes to one that the respondent State is to pay the applicant, within three months: (a) in respect of non-pecuniary damage, 10,000 pounds sterling; (b) in respect of costs and expenses, 15,000 pounds sterling plus VAT; and (c) simple interest at 8% per annum on these sums from expiry of the three months until settlement
holdings.reasoning_summary: The Court awarded just satisfaction for non-pecuniary damage and costs, reflecting the violations found under Articles 3 and 13.
